summary: This component renders a blog post item with different content depending on whether you're viewing a single post or a list of posts. When viewing a full post, it shows extra elements like related posts, social sharing, and user interaction widgets; when viewing a list, it only shows the basic post preview. The component uses Docusaurus's blog plugin to determine the viewing context.

explanations.24: This helper function checks whether we're on a full blog post page or a list view, and returns a CSS class name only for list view to add spacing between post cards.
explanations.25: The useBlogPost hook is a Docusaurus function that gives us information about the current blog context, including whether we're viewing a single post or a list.
explanations.26: The ternary returns a margin class name if we're NOT on a full post page (meaning we're in list view), otherwise returns undefined so no extra spacing is added.
explanations.33: This renders the AI icon badge only if two conditions are both true: the post's front matter says it was AI-assisted AND we're viewing the full post page (not a list card).
explanations.36: Similar logic to the AI icon: article action buttons only make sense on the full post page, so we only create this element if isBlogPostPage is true.
explanations.40: The clsx function combines multiple CSS class names together, keeping any undefined or falsy values out of the final string.
explanations.48: The TranslationNotice banner is deliberately placed outside the markdown content area so translators can't accidentally modify it, and it's only shown on the full post page.
explanations.53: This entire section with RelatedPosts, Bluesky, TypoReport, and Reaction widgets only renders when viewing the full post page, not when browsing the list view.
explanations.66: This renders the TriedIt component unless the front matter explicitly sets tried_it to false, allowing posts to opt out of this widget.
